quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. This warns the driver that you are about to slow down. It alerts them to hazards ahead that they may not see. Flashing is also helpful when slowing down suddenly on roads where drivers don't expect it.

questions.question: What should you do on a long trip?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride.
Ride more than 12 hours in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit yourself to no more than six hours of riding per day. Take rest breaks every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine because extreme fatigue will happen when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve itself. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out to be more visible.
Stay close together to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to be more visible.
questions.explanation: Staying close together makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Keep close ranks while leaving enough space around each rider to maneuver safely. Riding in pairs does not leave enough space for riders to move.

questions.question: Where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Where you are most likely to be seen and can keep a space cushion around yourself.
Where you can draft off other vehicles.
Where you can change lane positions most often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you are most likely to be seen and can keep a space cushion around yourself.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where you are most visible to other drivers and have adequate space around you for safety.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of distance behind the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to see that the vehicle has stopped and to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid hazards on the road surface.
Block your access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots and road hazards, and discourages other drivers from sharing your lane. Most importantly, it keeps an escape route available if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do?

options.text: Reduce speed when riding at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam headlight unless following or meeting another vehicle. Be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Anywhere, as they do not need to reach the footrests.
Holding onto the motorcycle frame only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may not balance properly and could get in the way of the operator's controls.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of the following do you NOT need to adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger sits lower and differently. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlights, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust brake light position.

questions.question: How long can the effects of marijuana last?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana starts working within minutes and lasts two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over one hour to start working but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing down, it means the rider is slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen the most?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, yellow, red, or green. These are much better than dark or dull colors for being seen.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action first, then the other
Brake and swerve at the same time
Choose to either brake or swerve
Only use the front brake and do not swerve

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions—do not do them at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause the motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: If it starts raining while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Pull onto the shoulder of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake lights before you slow down to warn the other driver
Pull over to the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake lights before you slow down to warn the other driver
questions.explanation: Flash your brake lights before slowing down. This warns the tailgater. The driver following you may not see hazards ahead, so give them a warning.

questions.question: What may you need to adjust when carrying a passenger?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. You may need to adjust the shocks. Also adjust the headlights and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Block all air from passing through
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield has no scratches, resists damage, allows clear side vision, fastens securely, lets air pass through to prevent fogging, and allows room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids wind blasts and other drivers' blind spots, and gives you an escape route. It should also discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.
